items.text: An applicant has completed 55 semester hours of undergraduate credit and wants to start law school this fall. Does BLE Rule 1(C) allow it?

B. No, Rule 1(C) requires at least 60 semester hours (or 90 quarter hours) before entering law school — Rule 1(C) sets a 60 semester hour (or 90 quarter hour) floor before entering law school, not a completed degree; 55 hours falls short.
A candidate wants to apply for the July bar exam but missed the March 1 regular deadline. What is the last day a late application will be accepted?
C. May 15 — Rule 2(A) sets the regular July-exam deadline at March 1 and the late-filing cutoff at May 15.
An applicant has a felony conviction from 8 years ago that was never reversed or vacated. Under BLE Rule 2(C), what must the applicant do?

A. Disclose the conviction and comply with the character and fitness committee's requests — Rule 2(C) requires disclosure of any conviction carrying possible incarceration that has not been reversed or vacated, with no age cutoff stated, and compliance with the committee's process.
What score must an applicant earn on the MPRE to satisfy Michigan's requirement?
C. 85 — Michigan's minimum passing MPRE score is 85, as confirmed on the NCBE Michigan jurisdiction page.
A candidate sits for the UBE in Michigan but only completes the MBE and MEE portions, skipping the MPT, in a single sitting. What happens to their score's portability?

D. They lose the ability to earn a score transferable to other UBE jurisdictions, because Rule 3(C) requires all components in a single administration — Rule 3(C) requires sitting for all UBE components in a single administration to earn a portable score transferable to other jurisdictions.
Which of the following is required before an attorney can be admitted to practice in Michigan by transferred UBE score, by UBE exam, or by admission without examination?

A. Completion of any Michigan Law Component course required by the Board — Rule 3a requires the Michigan Law Component before admission under any of the three listed paths: UBE exam, transferred UBE score, or admission without examination.
A candidate passed the Michigan UBE 3 years and 2 months ago and has not yet been admitted. Is that score still valid?
C. No, a passing score is valid for only 3 years — Rule 4(D) states a passing bar examination score is valid for three years; at 3 years and 2 months it has expired.
An applicant wants to transfer a UBE score of 265 earned in another UBE jurisdiction to Michigan. Can they, given Michigan's minimum score of 268?

B. No, Rule 4a(A)(1) requires the transferred score to meet or exceed Michigan's minimum required score — Rule 4a(A)(1) requires the applicant's score to meet or exceed the Board's minimum required score; 265 falls short of Michigan's 268.
An attorney licensed in Illinois wants Michigan admission without examination. Which two BLE rules must the attorney still independently satisfy?

A. Rules 1 and 2(B) (pre-law credit hours and reputable-and-qualified law school) — Rule 5(B)(1) requires an applicant for admission without examination to independently qualify under Rules 1 and 2(B).

An out-of-state attorney has actively practiced law as a principal occupation for only 2 of the past 5 years, with no teaching or JAG service in the other 3. Do they qualify for admission without examination under Rule 5(B)(5)?

D. No, absent a good-cause extension, Rule 5(B)(5) requires qualifying activity in 3 of the preceding 5 years — Rule 5(B)(5) requires active practice, full-time teaching, or JAG service in 3 of the preceding 5 years, though the Board may extend the period for good cause.
What is the current BLE fee for a first-time online UBE examination application, and how must first-time takers pay it?
B. $400, by credit card for first-time takers — Rule 6(A) and (D) set the UBE exam fee at $400, and require online bar examination payments for first-time takers to be made by credit card.
NCBE describes NextGen as testing what, compared to the legacy exam's separate MBE, MEE, and MPT components?

C. Nine areas of legal doctrine alongside seven foundational lawyering skills, integrated rather than tested in separately labeled components — NCBE describes NextGen as testing nine areas of legal doctrine alongside seven foundational lawyering skills, rather than the legacy exam's separately labeled MBE/MEE/MPT structure.
Four subjects were dropped from the MEE effective with the July 2026 bar exam. Which of the following was NOT one of them?

C. Civil Procedure — The four subjects dropped effective July 2026 are Conflict of Laws, Family Law, Trusts and Estates, and Secured Transactions. Civil Procedure remains on NCBE's current eight-area MEE list.
On the MEE Evidence outline, 'insurance coverage' is listed under which heading?

A. Privileges and other policy exclusions — The MEE outline lists 'Insurance coverage' as an item under 'Privileges and other policy exclusions.' Michigan's own rule is MRE 411: evidence that a person was or was not insured is not admissible to prove the person acted negligently or otherwise wrongfully.

A restoration contractor's adjuster verbally tells a homeowner the whole roof is covered, but the signed appraisal agreement lists only two slopes and contains a merger clause. Under Michigan's parol evidence rule, what happens if the homeowner sues for the whole roof based on the phone call alone?

D. The signed, unambiguous writing controls; the oral promise cannot vary it absent fraud invalidating the integration clause — UAW-GM v KSL holds parol evidence of a prior or contemporaneous oral promise cannot vary a clear, unambiguous written contract with a valid merger clause, except for fraud invalidating the integration clause itself.

A policyholder's disability claim is wrongly delayed for a year. Under Kewin v Massachusetts Mutual Life Ins Co, can the policyholder recover damages for the emotional toll of the delay as an ordinary contract-damages item?

B. No, Hadley v Baxendale limits ordinary contract damages to the contract's value, absent a Stewart-type life-and-death exception — Kewin applies Hadley v Baxendale to cap ordinary contract damages at the contract's value; the Stewart v Rudner exception for life-and-death contracts does not extend to an ordinary disability policy.

An insurer denies a third-party injury claim, arguing the insured lied on the application about a suspended license, a fact the insurer could have checked before issuing the policy. Under Titan Ins Co v Hyten, does the insurer's fraud defense fail because the fraud was easy to check?

A. No, Titan overruled the 'easily ascertainable' rule; the fraud defense survives even against an easily-checkable fact and an injured third party — Titan v Hyten expressly overruled the Court of Appeals' 'easily ascertainable' rule from Kurylowicz; an insurer's fraud defense is not defeated merely because the fraud was easy to discover.

A customer slips on an open and obvious patch of ice in a store parking lot. Under current Michigan law after Kandil-Elsayed v F & E Oil (2023), how is the open-and-obvious nature of the hazard analyzed?

D. It is weighed as part of breach and comparative fault, a jury question, not as part of duty — Kandil-Elsayed overruled Lugo's treatment of open-and-obvious as part of duty; it is now analyzed as part of breach and Michigan's comparative-fault statutes, a jury question.
A claimant wants to sue an insurer for an ordinary breach-of-contract dispute not covered by any more specific statute. Under MCL 600.5807, what is the applicable limitations period?
C. 6 years — MCL 600.5807(9) sets a 6-year limitations period for a breach-of-contract action not described in the section's other, more specific subsections.
Michigan's May 1, 2024 amendment to MRE 702 requires the proponent of expert testimony to show what?

B. That it is more likely than not that the admission factors are satisfied, and that the expert's opinion reflects a reliable application of principles and methods to the facts — The May 2024 amendment, ADM File No. 2022-30, requires a more-likely-than-not showing that the admission factors are satisfied and clarifies that the expert's opinion must reflect a reliable application of principles and methods. Federal Rule of Evidence 702, amended effective December 1, 2023, now reads the same way, but the Michigan order does not say it was copying it.
